map.Lessons 6-3, 6-4 & 6-5 — exponents, orde: Lessons 6-3, 6-4 & 6-5: exponents, order of operations, and algebraic expressions. Four reader gates stand between the crew and the vault's second ring.
map.Previously: the vault's FIRST ring fell: Last time: the vault's FIRST ring fell to honest quotients. The glitch ran one ring deeper. Status: it is still terrible at math.
map.Previously, in Axiom City: a scribble ma: Last time, in Axiom City: a scribble made of broken equations locked Ada Vex's cipher vault and scrambled every sign in town. The crew split its fraction lies. Twelve quarter-meter strips hide inside three meters of ribbon, thank you very much. The first ring rolled open. Two rings to go. The glitch went down the stairs giggling.
map.Ring two: a giant dial of glowing powers: Ring two: a giant dial of glowing powers. This is a puzzle BOSS DOOR and I have never been happier.
map.The second ring is a dial of powers — li: The second ring is a dial of powers: little expressions like 2⁶ and 5³. Each notch only glows when it gets its true value. The glitch makes every number bigger by reading exponents wrong.
map.Andre unrolls chalk and a plan. Mateo ho: Andre unrolls chalk and a plan. Mateo holds the lantern. The glitch jeers from the dark.
map.Practice chip: 10³. Base 10, exponent 3: Practice chip: 10³. Base 10, exponent 3, so three 10s multiplied. One thousand.
map.A power has two parts: the base — the nu: A power has two parts: the base, the number being copied, and the exponent, the count of copies being MULTIPLIED. Never base times exponent. That mistake is the glitch's whole personality.
map.Say 10³ \"ten to the third power.\" The: Say 10³ "ten to the third power." The exponent counts factors. It is not a number to multiply by: 10 × 10 × 10 = 1000, while the glitch's 10 × 3 = 30 is nowhere close.
map.Reader — feed the first two notches thei: Reader, feed the first two notches their TRUE values. The glitch already smeared its little "12" on one. Write over it.
Two dark notches on the ring: 2⁶ and 5³. The glitch smeared its "answers", 12 and 15, across them. Feed each notch its TRUE value.
map.Conceptual: a power is repeated MULTIPLI: Conceptual: a power is repeated MULTIPLICATION. The base is the number being copied. The exponent counts the copies. It never means base × exponent. That is the glitch's whole personality.
map.Procedural: write the base again and aga: Procedural: write the base again and again with × between. Write as many copies as the exponent says. Then multiply step by step, left to right.
map.It turned one click and JAMMED. The next: It turned one click and JAMMED. The next notch isn't a single power. It's a whole line of math.
map.The order of operations: parentheses fir: The order of operations: parentheses first. Exponents second. Multiplication and division third, together, left to right. Addition and subtraction last. Andre's chalk test: 5 + 2 × 3² becomes 5 + 2 × 9. Multiplication goes next, and the line ends at 23.
map.Reading 5 + 2 × 3² straight left to righ: Reading 5 + 2 × 3² straight left to right blows it up to 63. That is exactly the kind of inflation the glitch loves. Rank order keeps numbers honest.
map.Notch III feeds the dial whole lines of: Notch III feeds the dial whole lines of math. It only turns when each line is read in the right ORDER. Evaluate: 4 + 3 × 2² and 36 ÷ (2 + 4) × 3.
map.Conceptual: an expression is read by RAN: Conceptual: an expression is read by RANK, not left to right. Parentheses first, then exponents, then multiplication and division together, then addition and subtraction at the very end.
map.Procedural: settle the parentheses, rewr: Procedural: do the parentheses. Write any power as its value. Then sweep ONCE left to right, doing every × and ÷ as you meet it. Addition waits for the end.
map.Two clicks down. Set into the ring: a br: Two clicks down. Set into the ring: a brass plate stamped with Ada Vex's handwriting. Words, not numbers.
map.Word-to-symbol translation. n is the var: Word-to-symbol translation. n is the variable, the mystery number in a costume. I write the expressions. Reader runs them.
map.Careful — \"less than\" is sneaky. It fl: Careful. "less than" is sneaky. It flips the order of what you write.
map.Andre's warm-up: \"4 more than three tim: Andre's warm-up: "4 more than three times m" becomes 3m + 4. The 3 is the coefficient, the number multiplying the variable. Feed it m = 2 and the machine gives 3 × 2 + 4 = 10. Value in, number out. That is evaluating.
map.An algebraic expression is math with at: An algebraic expression is math with at least one variable. "Times" makes a coefficient. "More than" adds after. "Less than" subtracts FROM the thing you built.
map.Reader — translate Ada's plate into symb: Reader, turn Ada's plate into symbols, then run the machine. The glitch is mouthing wrong answers at you. Rude.
map.The brass plate reads: \"the key is 7 le: The brass plate reads: "the key is 7 less than twice n." First pick the expression that says it in symbols. Then run it at n = 6 to get the key.
map.Conceptual: 'less than' is sneaky — it f: Conceptual: 'less than' is sneaky. It flips the order. '7 less than SOMETHING' means build the something first, then take 7 away from it. 'Twice' makes a coefficient of 2.
map.Procedural: two moves — write 'twice n': Procedural: two moves. Write 'twice n' as 2 times the variable, then subtract 7 from THAT whole thing. To evaluate, swap the variable for its value and follow the order of operations.
map.Three clicks. One alignment left. The gl: Three clicks. One alignment left. The glitch stops jeering and starts TOUCHING things.
map.It's rewriting the counterweight readout: It's changing the counterweight readouts! It just told the ring that 6² is 12, and the needle MOVED.
map.Analysis confirmed: the creature cannot: Analysis done: the creature cannot square. It multiplies the base by the exponent, then makes everything else bigger to hide it. Use TRUE values on the final alignment and the ring will reject every number it touched.
map.Boss Gate: turn the second ring — evalua: Boss Gate: turn the second ring. Evaluate the core, evaluate the counterweight, and stop the glitch's favorite lie for good.
map.BOSS GATE. Three locks. Feed the ring tr: BOSS GATE. Three locks. Feed the ring truth and it turns. Feed it glitch math and we live in a vault now.
map.Conceptual: in a term like 3x², the expo: Conceptual: in a term like 3x², the exponent grips ONLY the variable. Square first, then multiply by the coefficient. And parentheses are a package: finish the inside before anything multiplies them.
map.Procedural: Lock 1 — square the value of: Procedural: Lock 1: square the value of x, then triple the result. Lock 2: add inside the parentheses, then multiply by 5. Lock 3: remember what an exponent COUNTS.
And look what it opened onto… two doors. They wear two different expressions. That can't be an accident.
map.Power.A base and an exponent. The base i: Power.A base and an exponent. The base is the number being copied. The exponent counts the copies being MULTIPLIED. 10³ = 10 × 10 × 10 = 1000, never 10 × 3.
map.Order of operations.Read math by rank, n: Order of operations.Read math by rank, not left to right: parentheses, then exponents, then × and ÷ together, left to right, then + and − last.
map.Variable & coefficient.A variable is a l: Variable & coefficient.A variable is a letter for a number. A coefficient is the number multiplying it. "Less than" flips the order: build the thing first, then subtract from it.
map.The glitch's lie.Every inflation was the: The glitch's lie.Every wrong answer was the same move: base × exponent. An exponent counts factors. x² means x · x. Case closed.
map.completed Unit 6 · Episode 2: The Power: finished Unit 6 · Episode 2: The Power Ring and showed mastery of exponents, the order of operations, and writing and evaluating algebraic expressions.
map.Episode 3 — The Twin Doors — is waiting: Episode 3, The Twin Doors, is waiting at the bottom of the stairs.
map.Andre's practice chip: 10³ — base 10, ex: Andre's practice chip: 10³, base 10, exponent 3. Say it 'ten to the third power.'
map.10 × 10 = 100, then 100 × 10 = 1000. The: 10 × 10 = 100, then 100 × 10 = 1000. The glitch's version, 10 × 3 = 30, is nowhere close.
map.Your turn — same idea, different numbers: Your turn. Same idea, new numbers:
map.Andre's chalk warm-up: 5 + 2 × 3². No pa: Andre's chalk warm-up: 5 + 2 × 3². No parentheses, so the exponent goes first: 3² = 9.
map.The line now reads 5 + 2 × 9. Multiplica: The line now reads 5 + 2 × 9. Multiplication outranks addition, so 2 × 9 goes next.
map.Add last — the line settles at 23. Readi: Add last. The line ends at 23. Reading it straight left to right instead blows it up to 63: glitch math.
map.Ada's practice plate: '4 more than three: Ada's practice plate: '4 more than three times m.' Start with 'three times m'. That is 3m, where 3 is the coefficient and m is the variable.
map.Test-run it at m = 2: 3 × 2 + 4 = 10. Va: Test-run it at m = 2: 3 × 2 + 4 = 10. Value in, number out. The expression works like a machine.
map.Night-watch drill: 2y² at y = 3. Square: Night-watch drill: 2y² at y = 3. Square the variable first: 3 × 3 = 9. THEN the coefficient: 2 × 9 = 18. Squaring (2 × 3) instead gives 36, a different, wrong machine.
map.4(k + 5) at k = 2: parentheses first, 2: 4(k + 5) at k = 2: parentheses first, 2 + 5 = 7, then 4 × 7 = 28. The 4 waits outside until the inside is done.
map.And the glitch's favorite lie, retired:: And the glitch's favorite lie, retired: y² means y × y. An exponent counts copies of the base. It never multiplies by the exponent itself.
map.That's 2 × 6 — the glitch's signature mo: That is 2 × 6, the glitch's signature move. The exponent counts how many 2s get MULTIPLIED: six of them, no shortcuts.
map.That's 6² — base and exponent swapped co: That is 6². The base and exponent swapped places. In 2⁶ the 2 is the base being copied.
map.5 × 3 is glitch math. The exponent 3 cou: 5 × 3 is glitch math. The exponent 3 counts three 5s being multiplied. It is not a number to multiply by.
Notch I glows, but Notch II stays dark. Three copies of 5, multiplied. Not added, not times 3.
map.You added 4 + 3 first. Addition goes LAS: You added 4 + 3 first. Addition goes LAST. The exponent and the multiplication both come before it.
map.You multiplied 3 × 2 before squaring. Ex: You multiplied 3 × 2 before squaring. Exponents go BEFORE multiplication. Do 2² first.
map.Line A resists. Exponent first, then the: Line A resists. Exponent first, then the multiplication, then, at the very end, the addition.
map.You multiplied (2 + 4) × 3 before dividi: You multiplied (2 + 4) × 3 before dividing. Division and multiplication TIE. Sweep left to right: divide first, THEN multiply.
map.Line A glows — line B resists. Parenthes: Line A glows, but line B resists. Parentheses first, then ÷ and × left to right in one pass.
map.A = 16 and B = 18 — both lines read in p: A = 16 and B = 18. Both lines read in perfect rank. CLICK. CLICK. Two more notches blaze and the ring grinds on!
map.That says 'twice n less than 7' — the su: That says 'twice n less than 7'. The subtraction got flipped. Build twice n first, THEN take 7 away from it.
map.Those parentheses subtract inside first: Those parentheses subtract inside first. That machine doubles (n − 7), a different recipe from Ada's.
map.n² means n × n — nobody squared anything: n² means n × n. Nobody squared anything. 'Twice n' is the coefficient 2, not an exponent.
map.2n − 7 at n = 6: twice 6 is 12, minus 7: 2n − 7 at n = 6: twice 6 is 12, minus 7 is 5. The plate sinks flush into the ring. Key accepted!
map.Right symbols, wrong run — that's the fl: Right symbols, wrong run. That is the flipped expression's output. Double n FIRST, then subtract 7 from the result.
map.You subtracted inside parentheses that a: You subtracted inside parentheses that aren't there. Double n first. The 7 comes off at the end.
map.That's n² − 7 talking. 'Twice n' multipl: That is n² − 7 talking. 'Twice n' multiplies by 2. It never squares.
map.Swap n for 6, double it, then take 7 awa: Swap n for 6, double it, then take 7 away. Order of operations runs the machine.
map.Lock 1 holds. You squared (3 × 4) — but: Lock 1 holds. You squared (3 × 4), but the exponent grips ONLY the x. Square 4 first, THEN multiply by 3.
map.Lock 1 holds. x² is not x · 2. Square th: Lock 1 holds. x² is not x · 2. Square the 4, multiply it by itself, before the coefficient touches anything.
map.Lock 2 holds. That's 5 × 3 + 2 — but par: Lock 2 holds. That is 5 × 3 + 2, but parentheses are a package. Add n + 2 FIRST, then multiply the whole bundle by 5.
map.Lock 3 holds. That IS the glitch's lie —: Lock 3 holds. That IS the glitch's lie, the one that wrote 2⁶ = 12 on the wall. An exponent is a count, not a partner.
map.Lock 3 holds. x + x is 2x — doubling by: Lock 3 holds. x + x is 2x, doubling by addition. A power multiplies copies of the base instead.
map.Lock 3 holds. In x², the 2 sits up high: Lock 3 holds. In x², the 2 sits up high. It is an exponent counting copies, not a coefficient multiplying.
map.ALL LOCKS OPEN. Core 48, counterweight 2: ALL LOCKS OPEN. Core 48, counterweight 25, and the lie 'x² = x · 2' burns off the wall. The second ring TURNS, and below, two doors grind apart.
Yes! Now go back and open that gate.
map.Walk the steps above again — you've got: Go over the steps above again. You can do this.
